module_intro: Treats time as a filter at the intermediate level: the Asian range as reference, London Open Kill Zone, New York Open Kill Zone, London Close and other windows, session highs/lows as liquidity, session expansion/retracement/continuation/reversal, and kill-zone context/session selection (narrative first, time second).
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Requires Beginner Module 8 (Time & Trading Sessions), Beginner Module 9 (Power of 3), and Intermediate Modules 1-8.
module_objectives: Mark the Asian range and treat its high and low as primary intraday liquidity references.
Identify the London Open and New York Open Kill Zones and understand their typical behavioural roles.
Recognise the London -> New York relationship (manipulation then distribution / continuation).
Distinguish session expansion, retracement, continuation and reversal in real time.
Select the session (or kill zone) that best matches the higher-timeframe narrative.
Avoid trading low-probability windows simply because a PD array is present.
Integrate session timing with the multi-timeframe narrative established in Module 8.

concepts.name: The Asian Range as Reference
concepts.why_it_matters: The high and low of the Asian range become the most important intraday liquidity references for the London session. London frequently sweeps one side of the Asian range (the Judas Swing / manipulation) before reversing or continuing in the direction of the higher-timeframe narrative.

raw_sections.Character: The Asian session (commonly referenced in New York time as roughly 20:00 - 00:00 / 8:00 PM - 12:00 AM ET, with minor variation by source and DST) is primarily a range-building or accumulation window. Volatility is typically lower; price often consolidates into a defined high and low.
raw_sections.Practical Use: The high and low of the Asian range become the most important intraday liquidity references for the London session. London frequently sweeps one side of the Asian range (the Judas Swing / manipulation) before reversing or continuing in the direction of the higher-timeframe narrative.
raw_sections.Intermediate Discipline: The Asian range is marked for reference, not usually for aggressive directional trading. Chasing breakouts of the Asian range during Asia itself is a common low-quality behaviour.

raw_sections.Timing: The London Open Kill Zone is commonly cited as approximately 02:00 - 05:00 ET (New York time). Traders must adjust for daylight saving and confirm against their broker's server time.
raw_sections.Typical Behaviour:
London is frequently the first major liquidity event of the trading day for FX pairs. Characteristic behaviours include:

799. A sweep of the Asian range high or low (manipulation / Judas Swing),

800. Subsequent displacement and Market Structure Shift in the opposite direction or in the direction of the daily bias,

801. Creation of the PD arrays (FVG, Order Block) that will be used for entry on the retracement.
raw_sections.Role in the Narrative: When the higher-timeframe bias is clear, London often delivers the first high-probability expression of that bias after the Asian liquidity has been engineered.

raw_sections.Timing: The New York Open Kill Zone is commonly cited as approximately 07:00 - 10:00 ET (sometimes narrowed or extended depending on the source; many focus on 07:00 - 09:00 or include the 08:30 - 11:00 window that overlaps equity-market open). Again, confirm local and broker time.
raw_sections.Typical Behaviour: New York often continues or expands the directional move initiated in London, or delivers a second liquidity event and displacement if London was only the manipulation phase. The London - New York overlap is typically the highest-volume period of the day for many instruments.
raw_sections.Relationship to London: A frequent sequence is: Asian range builds liquidity -> London sweeps one side and establishes direction -> New York continues that direction or raids the opposite side and then continues. The intermediate student watches the relationship rather than treating each session in isolation.

raw_sections.London Close: A London Close window (often referenced around 10:00 - 12:00 ET) can produce profit-taking, reversals or continuation depending on the day's profile. It is secondary to the Open kill zones for most intermediate models.
raw_sections.Low-Probability Periods: Midday / lunch periods and late Asian hours are frequently low-conviction. Intermediate discipline is to stand aside rather than force setups in dead zones.

raw_sections.Session Extremes as Liquidity: Each session prints its own high and low. These extremes become intraday buy-side and sell-side liquidity pools. The Asian high/low are the most commonly raided; London and New York highs/lows become targets or further liquidity for later sessions or the next day.
raw_sections.Sequential Liquidity Across Sessions: Price may raid Asian liquidity in London, then target London extremes in New York, then leave New York extremes as the next day's Asian or London objectives. Mapping these sequential pools keeps the intraday Draw on Liquidity coherent.

concepts.name: Session Expansion, Retracement, Continuation and Reversal

raw_sections.Expansion: Session expansion is the forceful directional move that leaves displacement and PD arrays. It is the phase in which the session's true directional intent is expressed.
raw_sections.Retracement: After expansion, price often retraces into the PD arrays (FVG, Order Block, OTE) created by the expansion. This retracement is the preferred intermediate entry window.
raw_sections.Continuation: Continuation occurs when the session (or the next session) resumes in the direction of the prior expansion after the retracement, typically targeting the next liquidity pool.
raw_sections.Reversal: Session reversal occurs when the initial expansion is itself a manipulation (e.g., Judas Swing of the Asian range) and the true directional move is opposite. Distinguishing manipulation from genuine expansion requires the higher-timeframe narrative and the quality of the subsequent displacement and MSS.

raw_sections.Narrative First, Time Second: Session selection is subordinate to the multi-timeframe narrative (Module 8). The student first decides the directional story and the price zone of interest, then asks which kill zone is most likely to deliver that story.
raw_sections.Practical Matching:
802. Clear daily bias + Asian range ready to be swept -> London Open is often the first opportunity.

803. London has already established direction and left PD arrays -> New York Open may continue or refine the entry.

804. No clear narrative or conflicting signals -> stand aside regardless of the clock.
raw_sections.One-Session Focus: Many consistent intermediate practitioners specialise in a single kill zone (London or New York) rather than attempting to trade every window. Mastery of one window is preferable to mediocre coverage of all windows.

rules.statement: Asian session: commonly referenced as roughly 20:00-00:00 / 8:00 PM-12:00 AM ET, with minor variation by source and DST -- primarily a range-building/accumulation window with typically lower volatility.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Minor variation by source and DST.

rules.statement: London Open Kill Zone: commonly cited as approximately 02:00-05:00 ET (New York time). Traders must adjust for daylight saving and confirm against their broker's server time. London is frequently the first major liquidity event of the trading day for FX pairs: sweep of the Asian range high/low (manipulation/Judas Swing), followed by displacement and MSS.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: unspecified precise boundary; minor variation across sources.

rules.statement: New York Open Kill Zone: commonly cited as approximately 07:00-10:00 ET (sometimes narrowed to 07:00-09:00 or extended to include the 08:30-11:00 window overlapping the equity-market open). New York often continues or expands London's move, or delivers a second liquidity event and displacement if London was only the manipulation phase. The London-New York overlap is typically the highest-volume period of the trading day.

London Close window (often referenced around 10:00-12:00 ET) can produce profit-taking, reversals, or continuation depending on the day's profile -- secondary to the Open kill zones for most intermediate models. Midday/lunch periods and late Asian hours are frequently low-conviction; intermediate discipline is to stand aside rather than force setups in dead zones.

Frequent intraday sequence: Asian range builds liquidity -> London sweeps one side and establishes direction -> New York continues that direction or raids the opposite side and then continues. Session extremes become intraday buy-side/sell-side liquidity pools; price may raid Asian liquidity in London, then target London extremes in New York, then leave New York extremes as the next day's Asian or London objectives.

Kill-zone/session selection practical matching: clear daily bias + Asian range ready to be swept -> London Open is often the first opportunity. London has already established direction and left PD arrays -> New York Open may continue or refine the entry. No clear narrative or conflicting signals -> stand aside regardless of the clock. Session selection is subordinate to the multi-timeframe narrative: decide the directional story and price zone of interest first, then ask which kill zone is most likely to deliver that story.

examples.content:
HTF narrative: Daily bias bullish; price in discount relative to the daily dealing range; Draw on Liquidity is buy-side above a prior daily high.

Asian range: High 1.0850, Low 1.0800. Marked as primary intraday liquidity.

London Open: Price sweeps the Asian low (1.0795), then displaces higher with a clear MSS and leaves a bullish FVG / Order Block in discount. This is interpreted as manipulation of sell-side liquidity followed by bullish expansion.

Entry: Retracement into the London-created FVG / OTE during the remainder of the London kill zone or early New York.

New York: Continues the bullish expansion toward the daily buy-side objective. Partial profits at internal liquidity; remainder held toward the HTF target.

Invalidation: Decisive close back below the London displacement origin or the Asian low that was swept, depending on the exact structural reference chosen.
examples.interpretation_given_in_text: Demonstrates a London sweep of the Asian range followed by New York continuation, illustrating the sequential session liquidity model.

relationships.statement: The multi-timeframe narrative (Module 8) supplies direction and price zone. Sessions and kill zones supply the time window in which that narrative is most likely to be expressed. Asian range supplies the first liquidity. London and New York supply the manipulation and distribution phases. Expansion creates the PD arrays; retracement into those arrays (refined by OTE and CE) supplies the entry; continuation delivers the Draw on Liquidity. Trading outside the relevant kill zone is equivalent to ignoring a major filter.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Chasing breakouts of the Asian range during the Asian session itself is a common low-quality behaviour; the Asian range is marked for reference, not usually for aggressive directional trading. Do not force setups in low-conviction dead zones (midday/lunch, late Asian hours); stand aside instead.

key_terms: Asian range - consolidation high/low formed during the Asian session; primary intraday liquidity reference.
London Open Kill Zone - approximately 02:00 - 05:00 ET; often the first major liquidity event and displacement window.
New York Open Kill Zone - approximately 07:00 - 10:00 ET; frequently continues or expands the London direction.
Judas Swing - manipulative sweep (often of the Asian range) that precedes the true directional move.
Session expansion - forceful directional move that creates PD arrays.
Session retracement - return into the PD arrays created by expansion; preferred entry window.
Session continuation - resumption in the direction of the prior expansion after retracement.
Session reversal - true direction opposite to the initial session expansion (manipulation failure).
Kill-zone context - the requirement that high-quality setups preferably occur inside relevant institutional time windows.
module_review_notes.beginner_summary: Beginner teaching introduced sessions and kill zones as time windows. Intermediate teaching integrates those windows with the multi-timeframe narrative, treats the Asian range as a liquidity map, distinguishes manipulation from expansion, and makes session selection a deliberate filter rather than a habit of trading every hour.
module_review_notes.concept_relationships_summary: Narrative (Module 8) decides direction and zone. Sessions decide the time of highest probability. Liquidity (Module 2) is mapped onto session extremes. Displacement and MSS (Module 3) confirm the session's true intent. PD arrays and OTE (Modules 4 - 7) refine the entry on the retracement inside the kill zone.
module_review_notes.practical_chart_exercise:
For the next five trading days:

- Before London, mark the Asian range high and low.

- State the HTF narrative in one sentence and which kill zone is the primary candidate.

- During London, record whether the Asian range was swept and whether displacement + MSS followed.

- Note any PD arrays created and whether a retracement entry appeared.

- Observe New York's relationship to the London direction (continuation, reversal, or chop).

- End of day: write one paragraph on how well session behaviour matched the pre-session narrative and one improvement for the next day.
self_test_questions: Why is the Asian range marked even if the trader does not trade during Asia?
What is a Judas Swing and how does it relate to the Asian range?
Outline a common London -> New York relationship in a trending day.
How should the student respond to a clean-looking FVG that forms outside any kill zone?
What is the difference between session expansion and session manipulation?
Why might a trader specialise in only one kill zone?
common_misconceptions: "I must trade every kill zone." - False. One well-understood window is often superior.
"If London did nothing, New York will definitely reverse." - Not a rule; the HTF narrative still governs.
"Asian range breakouts are high-probability trades." - Usually the opposite; the range is more often liquidity for later sessions.
"Kill-zone times are exact to the minute on every broker." - Times vary with DST and server; confirm your own clock.
"A setup outside a kill zone is automatically invalid." - Overstated; probability is lower, not zero. Intermediate discipline still prefers the kill zone.
